items.definition:
a small vessel designed to operate underwater
The research team used a submersible to explore the ocean floor.

the suburbs or their inhabitants, especially considered as a cultural entity
Life in suburbia often involves commuting to the city for work.

a girl who enjoys rough, noisy activities traditionally associated with boys
She was a real tomboy, always climbing trees and playing sports.

a small increase or improvement
We've seen a slight uptick in sales this quarter.

a mischievous young child, or a sea creature
The little urchin ran off with the stolen apple.

a person who violates a rule or law
The police issued a ticket to the traffic violator.

work in progress
The new feature is still a WIP, but we expect it to be ready next week.

a type of wading bird with a long bill
The hunter spotted a woodcock hiding in the undergrowth.

year-over-year
The company reported a 10% YoY growth in sales.

a substance that makes a chemical reaction or process happen or happen more quickly
The enzyme acts as an activator for the reaction.

a room at the back of a building, often used for private or unofficial activities
The politicians held a secret meeting in the backroom.

a large, predatory, tropical marine fish
Divers spotted a barracuda swimming near the coral reef.

blind carbon copy (in email)
Remember to use BCC if you don't want recipients to see each other's email addresses.

a person from Belarus; the Belarusian language
She is learning Belarusian to communicate with her family.

the outer shell of a vehicle
The car needed extensive bodywork after the accident.

headgear used to control a horse
He put the bridle on the horse before riding.

an arthropod of the large class Crustacea, such as a crab, lobster, or shrimp
Lobsters and crabs are types of crustacean.

a defensive player in ice hockey or other sports
The defenceman blocked the shot with his stick.

A person who puts money in a bank.
The bank guarantees the safety of its depositors' funds.

A device that spreads light, sound, or scent.
She put a few drops of essential oil into the diffuser.

A genre of electronic music.
She prefers listening to electronica over rock music.

A long, open, level area, typically by the sea or a river, for walking.
We took a stroll along the esplanade at sunset.

The practice of giving unfair preferential treatment to one person or group.
The employees complained about the manager's favoritism.

The dominant social system in medieval Europe, in which the nobility held lands from the Crown in exchange for military service.
Feudalism was a complex system of land tenure and social hierarchy.

An unborn offspring, especially an unborn human baby more than eight weeks after conception.
The doctor monitored the development of the foetus.

A Japanese entertainer who performs various Japanese arts.
The geisha performed a traditional dance.

An open space in a forest.
Sunlight filtered through the trees into the peaceful glade.

A very helpful or valuable thing, person, or event.
The unexpected financial aid was a real godsend.

a doctor specializing in women's health
She made an appointment with her gynecologist for a check-up.

a person who makes or sells hats
The Mad Hatter is a famous character from Alice in Wonderland.

an electrical device that converts DC to AC
The solar panels are connected to an inverter to power the house.

a blow that knocks someone down; a type of house that can be assembled quickly
The boxer delivered a powerful knockdown in the third round.

a deep blue metamorphic rock used as a gemstone
The necklace was adorned with beautiful lapis lazuli stones.

a person who sets a person or place free from imprisonment or oppression
He was hailed as the liberator of his people.

a geometric design or pattern representing the cosmos or deities in various religions
She spent hours coloring the intricate mandala design.

a unit of power equal to one million watts
The new solar farm generates 50 megawatts of electricity.

(informal) a person's wife.
He asked his missus if she wanted tea.

a person who climbs mountains as a sport or profession.
The experienced mountaineer prepared for the ascent.

a grey alloy of tin with lead, copper, and other metals.
The old tankard was made of pewter.

(computing) a window or advertisement that appears suddenly on a computer screen; (general) something that appears suddenly.
I closed the annoying popup advertisement.

a state ruled by a prince
Monaco is a small principality on the French Riviera.

the final part of a joke
Everyone laughed when he finally delivered the punchline.

lack of regard for the danger or consequences of one's actions
His recklessness on the road led to an accident.

a round building or room, especially one with a dome
The museum's grand rotunda was filled with natural light.

a circular building for locomotives or a powerful circular kick
He delivered a powerful roundhouse kick to his opponent.

a type of beetle or an ancient Egyptian gem carved in its shape
The archaeologist discovered an ancient scarab beetle amulet.

a tool used for mowing grass or reaping crops
The farmer used a scythe to cut the tall grass.

a reddish-brown color associated with old photographs
The old photograph had a warm sepia tone.

comedy based on deliberately clumsy actions and embarrassing events
Charlie Chaplin was a master of slapstick comedy.

anxiety, discomfort
There was a general sense of unease in the room after the announcement.

period of time when a system is operational
The server had an impressive uptime of 99.9% last month.

Length or amount measured in yards
The tailor needed to calculate the exact yardage of fabric.

Energy, enthusiasm, or a sharp, high-pitched sound
The comedian's jokes had a real zing to them.

A hormone secreted by the adrenal glands, especially in conditions of stress
The sudden fright caused a rush of adrenalin.

the study of human history and prehistory through the excavation of sites and the analysis of artifacts
Archeology helps us understand ancient civilizations.

the area of land directly facing a beach
They bought a beautiful beachfront property.

the act of taking and using something that belongs to someone else with the intention of returning it
Her constant borrowing of money became a problem.

a type of spicy Spanish sausage
We had paella with chicken and chorizo for dinner.

a person from the East End of London, or their accent/dialect
His strong Cockney accent was difficult for some to understand.

a person who advocates for the protection of the environment and wildlife
The conservationist worked tirelessly to protect endangered species.

a narrow opening or fissure, especially in a rock or wall
A tiny plant was growing in the crevice of the old stone wall.

a friendly slap or handshake, especially as a greeting
He gave his friend a quick dap as they passed in the hallway.

a person who tries to avoid paying debts or responsibilities
He was tired of his roommate being a deadbeat and never paying rent.

the main dish of a meal (US English); a dish served before the main course (UK English)
For my entree, I chose the grilled salmon.
